obtained.how: open-access PDF from the publisher (SEAFWA's journal archive)

bibliography.checked_against: the article's first page and running heads
bibliography.note: Bevelhimer, M. S. 1995. Smallmouth bass habitat use and movement patterns with respect to reservoir thermal structure. Proc. Annu. Conf. Southeast. Assoc. Fish and Wildl. Agencies 49: 240–249. Printed page = PDF page + 239.

claims.claim: adults tracked in a Tennessee reservoir (12 tagged, 4 followed for activity)
claims.quote: Activity was analyzed for 4 fish with which I had direct tracking contact
claims.conditions: Melton Hill Reservoir, a 2,270-ha mesotrophic, thermally stratified Clinch River impoundment (71 km long, ≤ 0.6 km wide); 12 adults of 368–542 mm and 560–2,130 g, 6 tagged in 1986 and 6 in 1987; activity from the 4 most-tracked 1987 fish, 107 h of contact

claims.quote: Smallmouth bass were mobile about 6.7 hours/day
claims.conditions: 28 % of 24 h, 42 % of the daylight and twilight hours (~0530–2130), 'assuming movement at dark was minimal'; only 1 fish on 1 occasion was tracked between 2300 and 0600 (p. 243)
claims.note: The night was assumed, not measured; the rewrite could say so.

claims.quote: The average rate of movement for all smallmouth bass was 4.2 m/minute.
claims.conditions: four 1987 fish; individual rates 3.4, 4.7, 6.5 and 7.5 m/min (Table 1)
claims.note: The source's own averages are not the means of its four fish (those are 5.5 m/min and 2,096 m/day against the printed 4.2 and 1,243); the paper quotes the printed 4.2 correctly.

claims.quote: Estimates of distance moved ranged from 825 to 3,477 m/day (Table 1).
claims.conditions: estimated as the proportion of the day spent moving × rate of movement × 1,440 (p. 243), per fish

claims.quote: the estimated distance traveled both peaked in the afternoon and were minimal at night

claims.claim: adults stayed within 5 m of shore most of the time
claims.quote: 5 m of the shore most of the time regardless of the inshore temperature
claims.conditions: 'regardless of the inshore temperature'; fish tracked May–November 1987, temperature and depth reliable only through July; 1986 fish 'usually found in the littoral zone, even when inshore water temperatures exceeded 28 C'

claims.claim: usually in water under 2 m deep
claims.quote: they were usually near shore and in shallow (<2m depth) water
claims.conditions: from June to mid-July 1987 all fish were in the top 1.5 m of the water column (p. 244); whether '<2m depth' is bottom depth or fish depth is not said

claims.claim: they entered open water only to cross small embayments
claims.quote: Except for crossings of small embayments, smallmouth bass were not found in the open water

claims.claim: did not move between inshore and offshore water by day and night
claims.location: p. 244 (PDF p. 5), Results; p. 247 (PDF p. 8), Discussion
claims.quote: did not exhibit diel offshore/inshore movements among different habitats in response to temperature
claims.conditions: 22 fixes on 6 fish, June to mid-July 1987, with no significant change in temperature or depth within tracking sessions; nights barely sampled (one fish tracked 2300–0600 once)

claims.claim: rested beside fallen trees, logs and boulders
claims.quote: including fallen trees, submerged logs, boulders, overhanging bushes, and man-made fish attractors
claims.conditions: 'When smallmouth bass were not moving, they often were associated with structures visible from the surface'

notes: Every claim checks. Context the rewrite may want: Melton Hill is a long (71 km), narrow (≤ 0.6 km) river reservoir of 2,270 ha, not a small lake, and its narrow channel limits how far from shore a bass can be; §3.7.8's 'mostly from small lakes and reservoirs' fits it loosely. The bass stayed in warm (> 28 °C) shallow water although cooler, oxygenated water was available deeper, and 1987 was abnormally cool from mid-July (cold hypolimnetic releases), so only data before 17 July were used for temperature selection (p. 244). The 6.7 h/day assumes no movement at night. Other values: preferred temperature taken as 21–26 °C for adults (p. 241); estimated daily movement and observed shoreline range averaged 1,243 m and 1,258 m (Table 1); smallmouth less active at night except nest-guarding males (p. 247, citing Hinch & Collins 1991).
